content:
“Daily Show” host Jon Stewart on Monday looked at how it seems like “all of our nation’s critical systems are falling apart” after tech failures brought down air travel, email and banking within a matter of a few days.

Or as Stewart called it, “an advent calendar of societal collapse.”

President Donald Trump, naturally, blamed former President Joe Biden. Then he said last week’s FAA nationwide ground stoppage was caused by “very, very old equipment that had a heart attack.”

Stewart guessed that was exactly how someone explained the problem to Trump.

“Uh, you see, Mr. President, normally the system works great, but sometimes a plane can wake up, and its ankles are filled with fluid, and one of the wings has a really weird bruise on it,” Stewart said.

Stewart also noted that ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang may already be planning a comeback after multiple reported affairs ― including one with an alleged Chinese spy ― ended his tenure at the tech giant he co-founded.

Trump said he was OK with Huang returning to the company, which designs many of the chips that power artificial intelligence. He called Huang a “brilliant person” and, in another clip, described himself as a “cheerleader for geniuses,” while also arguing that the government shouldn’t regulate AI to ensure that the U.S. can compete with China.

But what’s really at stake?

Stewart rolled a clip of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman saying, “I don’t want to go back to a world where I had to, like, painfully kind of try to find things on my computer.”

Stewart reached into his pocket, where he found a response:

“We’ve got to leave you fucking geniuses alone and not go anywhere near what you’re designing and not try and regulate at all or we’ll all live in that pre-AI primitive environment of 2022,” Stewart snarked. “I mean, back then, if you wanted pizza near you, you had to hand-Google it.”

He noted that at least Google would give you a list of pizza places near you.

“The truth is, AI is really just Google on coke,” Stewart said, and showed a mock AI response about getting pizza, which wasn’t just a list of pizza places.

“Oh my God, pizza! Oh my God, that’s such a great idea!” Stewart read. “Oh my God, are you looking for Neapolitan or Sicilian? There’s so many great ― did you know pizza was started in Greece?”

Stewart eventually cut off the mock AI answer.

“Shut the fuck up!” he said.

“If we can’t exist as humans without us all being connected to this one box, well, maybe that future isn’t for us,” he added.
